newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.
newsitem.headline: DUTCH CLOSING SHARE MARKET REPORT.

text.p: Dutch shares finished lower on Tuesday, retreating from Monday's record high close in the face of a weaker Wall Street and lower bond prices.

"It went lower from the start with people pretty disappointed about Wall Street finishing off the top yesterday," said one dealer. "There wasn't any good news out of the bond market so people took a profit here and there," he added.

The AEX closed 4.55 points down at 648.29, sinking back below the 650 level which was crossed for the first time on Monday. Wall Street's lower opening, with the Dow Jones down some 30 points by the Dutch close, also dampened spirits.
"It's not really been a large sell off," said one dealer, adding, "People have just been taking a few profits and starting to look at puts in the options market."

Dealers said the market could be entering a consolidation phase after breaking back below the first record high of the year. "I think people are expecting the market not to go anywhere special for a while," said one trader.

He said investors could be getting ready to settle back and wait for trends emerging from the 1996 full-year reporting season before investing whole-heartedly although many analysts expect the AEX will finish this year with a 10 percent gain.

"When you look at the charts it looks like we're having some problems holding onto the 650 level although people are talking about 660 being the trigger for a big sell-off," said another trader, highlighting the chance of a medium-term consolidation.

Music and movies group PolyGram bucked the overall trend, climbing 2.50 guilders to 87.20. One dealer said the shares had looked oversold of late, while a couple of relatively minor deals on Tuesday had helped sentiment.
PolyGram said on Tuesday it bought a 25 percent stake in the main part of a Turkish music firm, while Canal Plus of France said it signed a pay TV deal with PolyGram Filmed Entertainment.

Steel and aluminium maker Hoogovens fell 1.60 guilders to 70.30, slipping before news published after the bourse closing that its German aluminium subsidiary had agreed to buy France's Pechiney-Batiment's Alfal unit for an undisclosed price.

Vendex closed 80 cents lower at 81.00, reversing an early 80 cent gain made as a follow-through to Monday's 5.00 guilder gain on news of a French acquisition and plans for separate retail and services listings.
Unilever slipped 4.30 guilders to 300.00 but dealers said this appeared overdone. Other leaders saw Philips down 0.50 guilders to 69.40. -- Keiron Henderson, Amsterdam Newsroom +31 20 504 5000
